visual.general_description: Twelve-lead electrocardiogram printout of the index patient.
visual.detailed_description: Twelve-lead electrocardiogram on light gray grid paper with a longer rhythm strip along the bottom. Printed text at the upper left is a Chinese-language examination time label with a date and clock time, and at the upper right a Chinese-language label whose value area is empty. Lead labels I, II, III, AVR, AVL and AVF run down the left column, V1 to V6 down the right column, and the bottom strip is labelled II. A rectangular calibration pulse starts each row, and short red vertical marks sit at the column boundary beside the V labels. The tracings show regularly spaced QRS complexes; the limb-lead rows have small deflections, while the V2 and V3 rows have deeper downward deflections and the V1, V2, V5 and V6 rows have broad rounded upward waves after the QRS. No axis values or scale text are visible.

visual.general_description: Planar and tomographic 99mTc-PYP scintigraphy of the index patient.
visual.detailed_description: Composite nuclear imaging figure. The top row has two grayscale planar images on a pale lavender header bar, with header text reading "1h ANT" and "2.5h ANT" followed by date text. Each shows diffuse speckled gray uptake over the chest; in the left image a darker oval region lies in the lower middle, and in the right image a dark vertical band runs through the centre with a darker patch at the lower middle. Below is a colour tomographic slice display on a black background using an orange, yellow, purple and blue scale: a first block of ring-shaped slices numbered from 8 to 35 in two rows under the heading "SA", a second block numbered from 52 to 79 in two rows under "HLA", and the top of a third block under "VLA" cut off at the lower edge. Slice shapes shrink toward each end of each series. Side text includes orientation words Septal, Lateral, Anterior, Inferior, Apex and Base and text reading "Rest [Recon - AC]", with a study date and time and a short site code at the upper right.
